the positron fraction data is consistent with the annihilation of dark matter particles with a mass of 1.2 TeV, annihilating into tau+tau−, but that the gamma ray flux from the galactic center and the antiproton fraction are not compatible with such a model.
the positron excess is not due to dark matter annihilation in the galactic halo, but rather to astrophysical sources.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the interpretation of the positrons as Dark Matter annihilations requires the introduction of additional astrophysical ingredients, which are not well constrained by current data.
